The rider's account - 'at least 1 km more' - is therefore not an assertion that needs corroboration from elsewhere; it is the platform's own figure.

The driver's counterstatement that the distance was 'about the same' is contradicted by the record it comes from. The trip record logs a route_deviation_detected at Yishun Avenue 1 / Yio Chu Kang Road and a route_rejoined at Sengkang West Avenue / Jalan Kayu, and the GPS trace runs on Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu from 13:27:45 to 13:35:45, on a route the record itself describes as recommended via Seletar Road. The deviation is a recorded fact of this trip, not a matter of the rider's impression.

There is no traffic justification for leaving the recommended route. The LTA traffic artifact covering the recommended segment - Seletar Road, Yishun Avenue 1 to Sengkang West Avenue, both directions, valid 12:51 to 14:21 and so overlapping the trip window - records no incident, roadwork or closure, with speed bands 5-6, and the derived result is justifies_reroute false with type NONE; the artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and was retrieved by the platform rather than supplied by a party. POL-RD-23 makes congestion, an incident or a closure the only justifications, and it says in terms that a driver's assertion with no such data does not justify a reroute - which is all the driver offers here ('Jalan Kayu road is smoother'). Rows (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-24 are therefore unavailable to the driver.

The driver also never told the rider he was leaving the recommended route. The chat log for this trip carries 0 messages and the trip record lists no in-app calls, and no call recording is in the record at all. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation - a brief reason is enough, but something is required - and a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established. Nothing in this record shows the rider agreed to the longer route, so the 'rider informed and agreed' limb of POL-RD-24 never opens and the rider's objection stands unaddressed by the driver.

The rider paid for the extra kilometre rather than merely observing it: the trip was metered on distance, with distance_charged_km of 8.3 at the 0.72 SGD per-km rate producing a distance fare of 5.98 SGD inside the 12.65 SGD total, while the recommended route was 7.3 km. POL-RD-23 makes congestion, an incident or a closure the only justifications, and it says in terms that a driver's assertion with no such data does not justify a reroute - which is all the driver offers here ('Jalan Kayu road is smoother'). Rows (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-24 are therefore unavailable to the driver.

The driver also never told the rider he was leaving the recommended route.
